title: Tensor kernels of finite submodule inclusions are eventually killed in flat quotient towers
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $(M_n)_{n\geq0}$ a tower of $A$-modules with $A$-linear transition maps. Assume $M_n$ is an $A/I^{n+1}$-module compatibly with its $A$-action and is flat over $A/I^{n+1}$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $P$ be a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $K\subseteq P$ a submodule. For every $n$ there is $m\geq n$ such that the transition $K\otimes_A M_m\to K\otimes_A M_n$ kills $\ker(K\otimes_A M_m\to P\otimes_A M_m)$. No surjectivity of the transitions is assumed.

source.place: Proofs of Tags 0911 (lemma-tor-strictly-pro-zero) and 0912 (lemma-limit-flat), at the presentation-kernel level; Artin--Rees is Algebra Tag 00IN. Verified online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0911 and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0912.

proof.text: Fix a finite A-module P and K ⊆ P. Artin--Rees gives c such that K ∩ I^(n+c+1)P ⊆ I^(n+1)K for every n. Take m=n+c, J=I^(m+1), S=A/J.

The base-changed inclusion f:S ⊗ K → S ⊗ P has kernel represented by k ∈ K with k ∈ JP. Indeed the quotient-tensor equivalences identify 1 ⊗ k with k mod JK, and 1 ⊗ k maps to zero exactly when k ∈ JP. Every element of S ⊗ K has such a representative.

Flatness of M_m over S makes M_m ⊗ ker f → M_m ⊗ (S ⊗ K) → M_m ⊗ (S ⊗ P) exact. Quotient cancellation and tensor symmetry identify the last map with K ⊗ M_m → P ⊗ M_m. The cancellation maps commute with that inclusion: on generators a ⊗ (s ⊗ k), both routes give sa ⊗ k.

An element in the tensor kernel therefore lifts to M_m ⊗ ker f. For each pure tensor a ⊗ [k] in this lift, Step 2 puts k ∈ K ∩ JP, and Step 1 puts k ∈ I^(n+1)K. The transition image is k ⊗ p_mn(a)=0: express k as a finite sum of ideal multiples, move the scalars to M_n, and use its quotient action. Tensor induction and additivity prove vanishing for the whole lift. This argument uses no surjectivity.
